---
title: "Data Infrastructure"
sidebarTitle: "Overview"
description: "The engines that get your data in and shape it — Airhouse, Airlayer, and Airform"
---

Data Infrastructure is the foundation of Oxygen: it gets your data in, shapes it,
and compiles it into the queries your [World Model](/guide/build/world-model) and
agents run. Three engines do the work, each open where it makes sense to be.

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="Airhouse" icon="warehouse" href="/airhouse">
    The managed warehouse and connector. It has its own documentation in the
    Airhouse tab.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Airlayer" icon="layer-group" href="/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airlayer">
    The **core of the World Model** — an in-process semantic engine that compiles
    YAML schemas into dialect-specific SQL. Open source.
  </Card>
  <Card title="Airform" icon="diagram-project" href="/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airform">
    dbt-style modeling — version-controlled SQL transforms that land clean,
    tested tables for the semantic model to build on. Open source.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## How they fit together

<Steps>
  <Step title="Land">
    Data arrives in **[Airhouse](/airhouse)** (or
    your own warehouse).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Shape">
    **[Airform](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airform)** models raw tables into
    clean, tested ones.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Compile">
    **[Airlayer](/guide/build/data-infrastructure/airlayer)** compiles your
    semantic definitions over those tables into correct SQL — the foundation the
    [World Model](/guide/build/world-model) reasons over.
  </Step>
</Steps>
